segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
And today we're talking about office stuff, things in your office.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论的是办公室的东西，你办公室里的东西。

segments.en: We are talking about secrets in the office or maybe specific little things that people talk about behind other people's back.
segments.zh: 我们正在谈论办公室里的秘密，或者人们背后谈论的特定小事。

segments.en: So this is an elementary level lesson.
segments.zh: 所以这是一节初级水平的课。

segments.en: Before we get going though, let's take a look at a phrase in today's vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 在我们开始之前，让我们看看今天词汇预览中的一个短语。

segments.en: So the phrase for today is actually the same as the title for this lesson and that's office gossip.
segments.zh: 所以今天的短语实际上与本课的标题相同，这就是办公室八卦。

segments.en: Okay, you all know what an office is.
segments.zh: 好吧，你们都知道什么是办公室。

segments.en: So to gossip means to talk about other people secretly or behind their backs or maybe talk about other people's problems or private things.
segments.zh: 所以说八卦意味着秘密地或背后谈论其他人，或者谈论其他人的问题或私人事物。

segments.en: So oh my God, did you hear?
John is totally going to break up with her.
segments.zh: 约翰完全要和她分手了。

segments.en: So you're talking about people without them knowing.
segments.zh: 所以你们是在别人不知情的情况下谈论他们。

segments.en: So you're talking about their private things, their relationships, maybe you're even maybe criticizing them.
segments.zh: 所以你在谈论他们的私人事物，他们的关系，也许你甚至可能在批评他们。

segments.en: So office gossip is talking about people in your office without them knowing.
segments.zh: 所以办公室八卦就是背着办公室里的人谈论他们。

segments.en: So saying bad things about them.
So without any more delay, why don't we listen to this dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 那我们不再耽搁，先来听第一遍这段对话吧。
最新的办公室八卦是什么？

segments.en: Well, you didn't hear this from me, but the rumor is Paula is getting a promotion.
segments.zh: 可别说是我告诉你的，听说宝拉要升职了。

segments.en: But she's a terrible worker and you can't trust her.
segments.zh: 但她是个糟糕的员工，你没法相信她。
她最会当面一套、背后一套。

segments.en: You can't believe anything she says.
segments.zh: 你不能相信她说的任何话。

segments.en: Hey guys, what are you two whispering about?
segments.zh: 嘿，你们两个在窃窃私语什么呢？

segments.en: Eric and I were just saying that you were the best person for the job.
segments.zh: 埃里克和我只是说你是这份工作的最佳人选。

segments.en: So we have four key words that we want to look at from this gossip dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以我们有四个关键词，要从这段八卦对话里来看。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at those now in Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不看看现在语言要点中的那些。

segments.en: Okay, the first word is rumor.
Now this is an interesting word about gossip.
segments.zh: 现在这是一个关于八卦的有趣词。

segments.en: So a rumor is a story that might or might not be true.
segments.zh: 所以谣言是一个可能是真的，也可能不是真的故事。

segments.en: Okay, so I heard a rumor that they broke up yesterday.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我听到了他们昨天分手的谣言。

segments.en: Okay, so you're not sure if they broke up or no one has told you for a fact.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你不确定他们到底分手没有，也没人确切地告诉过你。

segments.en: No, it means I probably heard it from someone else who heard it from someone else who heard it from someone else who doesn't really know.
segments.zh: 不，意思是这消息很可能是别人告诉我的，而那个人又是听别人说的，最后那个人其实也不清楚真相。

segments.en: So rumors are maybe guesses about people and you don't know if they're true.
segments.zh: 所以谣言可能是关于人的猜测，你不知道它们是否是真的。

segments.en: You see this a lot with famous people, movie stars.
segments.zh: 在名人、电影明星身上你经常能看到这种情况。

segments.en: They always talk about rumors that maybe they got married in secret or something.
segments.zh: 他们总是谈论可能是秘密结婚的谣言之类的。

segments.en: There's a rumor that Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt are breaking up.
segments.zh: 有传言说安吉丽娜·朱莉和布拉德·皮特要分手了。

segments.en: Okay, so we don't know if it's true.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们不知道这是不是真的。

segments.en: So now the rumor that they heard was that this girl Paula is getting a promotion.
segments.zh: 所以他们听到的传言是，这个叫宝拉的女孩要升职了。

segments.en: This is an important office word.
segments.zh: 这是一个重要的办公室词。

segments.en: This means to be offered a better job in your company.
segments.zh: 这意味着在公司里被提升到更好的职位。

segments.en: Alright, so this is a noun.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这是一个名词。

segments.en: Yes, I got a promotion last year which also meant I got more money.
segments.zh: 是的，我去年升职了，这也意味着我拿到了更多的钱。

segments.en: Now when they were talking about the promotion, the girl said, I can't believe, the guy said, and Eric said, I can't believe she's getting a promotion.
segments.zh: 现在当他们谈论晋升时，女孩说，我不敢相信，那家伙说，埃里克说，我不敢相信她会升职。
她真是当面一套，背后一套。

segments.en: So think about what this means.
segments.zh: 所以想想这意味着什么。

segments.en: To be two-faced means to have two different sides to your personality.
segments.zh: two-faced 意味着你的性格有两副面孔。

segments.en: A good one and a bad one.
So like, I can be very nice to Marco.
segments.zh: 就像，我可以对马可很好。

segments.en: Marco, wow, you look so good today.
segments.zh: 马可，哇，你今天看起来真好。

segments.en: And then, oh my God, Marco's such an idiot.
segments.zh: 然后，天哪，马可真是个白痴。

segments.en: He's like never working and he's always on the phone.
segments.zh: 他就像从不工作，他总是在打电话。

segments.en: Alright, so two-faced means to have two different sides to your personality.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以 two-faced 意味着你的性格有两副面孔。

segments.en: Now it's interesting the way that you use this word, you say two-faced, right?
segments.zh: 有意思的是这个词的用法，你说的是 two-faced，对吧？

segments.en: So you have to add the E-D at the end.
segments.zh: 所以你必须在最后添加 E-D。

segments.en: You can't say he is two-faced.
I don't like people who are two-faced.
segments.zh: 我不喜欢两面三刀的人。

segments.en: And we have one final word and it's actually a verb when people talk like this.
segments.zh: 我们有一个最后的单词，当人们这样说话时，它实际上是一个动词。
当他们这样说话的时候。

segments.en: So what are you whispering about?
So usually when people are whispering, they're talking about a rumor.
segments.zh: 所以通常当人们在窃窃私语时，他们在谈论谣言。

segments.en: You don't want somebody else to hear you.
So when you want to be very quiet, like at the movie theater, you whisper.
segments.zh: 所以当你想保持安静的时候，就像在电影院一样，你会耳语。

segments.en: So those are four words for language takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以这是语言要点的四个词。

segments.en: Why don't we go back, listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back to take a look at a couple of phrases.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不回去，再听一次对话，我们会回来看看几个短语。
最新的办公室八卦是什么？

segments.en: Well, you didn't hear this from me, but the rumor is Paula is getting a promotion.
segments.zh: 可别说是我告诉你的，听说宝拉要升职了。

segments.en: But she's a terrible worker and you can't trust her.
segments.zh: 但她是个糟糕的员工，你没法相信她。
她真是当面一套，背后一套。

segments.en: You can't believe anything she says.
segments.zh: 你不能相信她说的任何话。

segments.en: Hey guys, what are you two whispering about?
segments.zh: 嘿，你们两个在窃窃私语什么呢？

segments.en: Eric and I were just saying that you were the best person for the job.
segments.zh: 埃里克和我只是说你是这份工作的最佳人选。

segments.en: So now we have three key phrases from this great dialogue on Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以现在我们在流利表达栏目里，从这段精彩对话中学习三个关键短语。

segments.en: So this first one is the beginning to any great rumor.
segments.zh: 所以第一个是任何大谣言的开始。

segments.en: Have you heard that she got a promotion?
It's kind of, you're not really asking, right?
segments.zh: 这有点像是，你并不是真的在问，对吧？

segments.en: Although it is a question, have you heard?
segments.zh: 虽然是一个问题，你听说过吗？

segments.en: But you're not really expecting an answer.
segments.zh: 但你并没有真正期待答案。

segments.en: This means I'm going to tell you some gossip.
segments.zh: 这意味着我要告诉你一些八卦。

segments.en: Because maybe I did, maybe I didn't, but I'm still going to say it.
segments.zh: 因为也许我听说了，也许没有，但我还是要说出来。

segments.en: She's still going to say it anyway.
So usually you can say, what?
segments.zh: 所以通常你可以说，什么？

segments.en: Or in this case, Eric goes, no, go on, tell me.
segments.zh: 或者在这种情况下，埃里克说，不，继续，告诉我。
最新的办公室八卦是什么？

segments.en: So obviously he knows it's going to be gossip.
segments.zh: 很明显，他知道这将是八卦。

segments.en: And so the next thing Pam says is, well, you didn't hear this from me.
segments.zh: 所以帕姆接下来说的是：可别说是我告诉你的。

segments.en: This is a way of saying, okay, don't tell anyone that I told you.
segments.zh: 这是一种说法：好吧，别告诉任何人是我告诉你的。

segments.en: So you can tell people, but just don't tell them that I said that this happened because Pam doesn't want to get in trouble.
segments.zh: 所以你可以告诉别人，但别说是我说的，因为帕姆不想惹麻烦。

segments.en: She doesn't want anyone to know that she was giving out rumors.
segments.zh: 她不想让任何人知道她在散布谣言。

segments.en: So that's why she's starting out with, well, you didn't hear this from me, but the rumor is, okay.
segments.zh: 所以她才这样开头：可别说是我告诉你的，不过听说……

segments.en: So you can, so this is a way of saying, all right, don't tell anyone that I told you.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种说法：好吧，别告诉任何人是我告诉你的。

segments.en: You didn't hear this from me.
And also you can go, you can say, but the rumor is, or you can say, but rumor has it.
segments.zh: 你也可以说：不过听说……，或者：不过有传言说……

segments.en: Oh, rumor has it that Paula is getting a promotion.
segments.zh: 哦，有传言说宝拉要升职了。

segments.en: So you can go both ways.
And now he exclaimed something that's very strange.
segments.zh: 现在他说了一句很奇怪的话。

segments.en: If you just look at it from these two words, no way.
segments.zh: 如果你只是从这两个词看它，就不可能。

segments.en: Well, in this context, no way means really?
segments.zh: 嗯，在这个语境里，no way 的意思是“真的吗？”

segments.en: So it's a way to express surprise.
segments.zh: 所以这是一种表达惊讶的方式。

segments.en: But be careful because there's another meaning to this phrase.
segments.zh: 但要小心，因为这个短语还有另一个含义。

segments.en: For example, Marco, could you help me out and get the groceries from the car?
segments.zh: 例如，Marco，你能帮我从车上拿到杂货吗？

segments.en: But also if you say it like, no way, you're saying, wow, that's so interesting.
segments.zh: 但如果你用某种语气说 no way，意思就是“哇，这太有意思了”。

segments.en: So it can be an expression of surprise or it can be a way of saying no, very firmly, no way.
segments.zh: 所以它既可以表达惊讶，也可以表示坚定地拒绝——没门。
所以那里有三个很棒的短语。

segments.en: Very interesting dialogue about gossip, very common in the office environment.
segments.zh: 关于流言蜚语的非常有趣的对话，在办公环境中很常见。

segments.en: So why don't we listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back in a little bit.
segments.zh: 那我们再听一遍对话，一会儿再回来。
最新的办公室八卦是什么？

segments.en: Well, you didn't hear this from me, but the rumor is Paula is getting a promotion.
segments.zh: 可别说是我告诉你的，听说宝拉要升职了。

segments.en: But she's a terrible worker and you can't trust her.
segments.zh: 但她是个糟糕的员工，你没法相信她。
她真是当面一套，背后一套。

segments.en: You can't believe anything she says.
segments.zh: 你不能相信她说的任何话。

segments.en: What are you two whispering about?
Eric and I were just saying that you were the best person for the job.
segments.zh: 埃里克和我只是说你是这份工作的最佳人选。

segments.en: So office gossip is generally, well, it's common.
segments.zh: 所以办公室八卦一般是，嗯，这很常见。

segments.en: It happens in every office, but I think that it's good to avoid too much gossip because sometimes people's feelings can get hurt.
segments.zh: 它发生在每个办公室，但我认为避免过多的流言蜚语是件好事，因为有时人们的感情会受到伤害。

segments.en: It's actually very interesting because usually the bigger the company is, I think more gossip starts to spread because there are departments.
segments.zh: 这实际上非常有趣，因为通常公司越大，我认为更多的八卦开始传播，因为有部门。

segments.en: So you got the marketing department, the finance department.
So you're like, oh, Kathy from finance, she slept with Tom from marketing and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 你会说：哦，财务部的凯西，她跟市场部的汤姆睡了，之类的。

segments.en: Then you have the gossip about the bosses.
segments.zh: 然后还有关于老板的八卦。

segments.en: He totally left for the weekend, but his wife was at home.
segments.zh: 他周末明明外出了，可他老婆却在家。

segments.en: And also one of the situations where a lot of rumors and office gossip starts to come up is office parties or the office Christmas parties where people maybe are drinking or something happens and a lot of rumors start to spread.
segments.zh: 许多谣言和办公室八卦开始出现的情况之一是办公室派对或办公室圣诞派对，人们可能正在喝酒或发生了一些事情，许多谣言开始传播。

segments.en: And they're more relaxed than usual.
segments.zh: 而且他们比平时更放松。

segments.en: They do things they wouldn't normally do.
segments.zh: 他们做他们通常不会做的事情。

segments.en: So maybe we could open this up to you.
segments.zh: 所以也许我们可以把话题交给你们。

segments.en: Is there a common rumor or office gossip that you hear in your office?
segments.zh: 您是否在办公室听到了常见的谣言或办公室八卦？

segments.en: Or is there that one secretary or guy that's always spreading rumors and gossiping?
segments.zh: 还是有一位秘书或人一直在散布谣言和闲聊？

segments.en: And don't use any real names.
segments.zh: 并且不要使用任何真实名称。

segments.en: You can just tell us general stories.
segments.zh: 你可以告诉我们一般的故事。

segments.en: But that's about it for us here today at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 今天在 EnglishPod 就到这里了。

segments.en: Let us know if you have any questions or concerns.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何问题或疑虑，请告诉我们。
